episodes.204776: A thunderstorm developed over the City of Roanoke just before 6:45 pm EDT on August 21st, initially producing rainfall rates to nearly 5 per hour. Though the storm gradually weakened, it remained anchored over primarily the western half of the city through around 8:15 pm EDT before finally pushing away to the south.  While nearly all of the city received at least 2 inches of rain, the highest totals were over the Peters Creek basin, where a 4 to 5 bullseye stretched from the Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport (KROA) westward to S. Electric Road.  Both the airport and a personal weather station observed rainfall totals at the 1-hour and 2-hour durations that were 500-year rainfall events per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. By 8:00 pm EDT, CREST Unit Streamflow near the airport had peaked at just over 1,600 cfs/mi^2, with much of the western half of the city observing values ranging from 550 to 950 cfs/mi^2. FLASH 1-hour Average Recurrence Intervals peaked near Electric Drive at just under a 200-year event at 7:46 pm EDT.  Due to the rapid flooding of Peters Creek Road that runs alongside Peters Creek, the occupants of numerous vehicles required swift water rescues from emergency services personnel.  A Flash Flood Warning with a Base tag was issued at 7:29 pm EDT for the City of Roanoke, which was upgraded to a warning with a Considerable tag at 7:52 pm EDT when reports of swift water rescues began to come in.  After coordinating with the Emergency Manager of the City of Roanoke, the warning was upgraded to a Flash Flood Emergency with a Catastrophic tag at 9:02 pm EDT.
episodes.204789: A cluster of slow-moving thunderstorms passed across eastern Surry County and western Stokes County during the evening of August 21st.  Rainfall rates within some of the stronger storms were observed to be as high as 5 inches per hour. The FLASH 3-hour ARI in the Town of King was observed to be as high as a 20-year event at 11 pm EDT, while the 3-hour QPE/FFG ratio was observed reaching 105.

episodes.205498: A severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Pennington County in northwest MN during the evening. A cluster of storms moving into west central Minnesota also produced several brief weak landspout type tornadoes in Grant County, but produced no reported damage.

episodes.205793: On the afternoon and evening of August 22nd, 2025, a cold front pushing south across eastern Nebraska provided the focus for thunderstorm development. With sufficient instability (MLCAPE of 1500���2500 J/kg) and favorable bulk shear (30���40 kts), a few strong to severe storms developed across the region.||One storm in particular produced multiple hail reports. A public report noted a measured 1.25-inch hailstone northeast of Seward, Nebraska, at 3:43 PM CST, followed by another public report of 1-inch hail in Seward at 3:49 PM CST. As the storm tracked southward, a trained spotter reported additional 1-inch hail three miles south of Seward at 4:05 PM CST.||Farther south, radar imagery indicated a strong signature consistent with damaging winds. This was later confirmed by Emergency Management, who reported significant storm damage in the Dorchester, Nebraska area. Damage included roof damage to several structures, downed power lines, and flipped irrigation pivots. Based on radar estimates, this occurred between 4:46 and 4:48 PM CST, with wind speeds estimated at 80 mph. The storm continued southward through the evening before gradually weakening.
episodes.205970: Weak southwest to west steering flow combined with high atmospheric moisture and surface forcing from a weak trough and sea breezes produced localized heavy rainfall in the afternoon and evening over a diurnally unstable airmass.
episodes.206393: A ridge of high pressure remained overhead with moisture gradually increasing underneath the high pressure, resulting in hot temperatures and daily afternoon showers and thunderstorms. With the dry low layers, strong gusty outflow winds were the main concern with one particular thunderstorm producing a peak wind gust of 58 mph at the Rifle Garfield County Airport.
episodes.206570: The subtropical high was situated near the Four Corners area, producing an easterly steering flow of 15-20 kts across the region. Thunderstorm activity erupted near the Mogollon Rim during the early afternoon hours and was steered west to west-southwestward into the lower deserts of south-central AZ, where new thunderstorm activity developed along outflow boundaries. With MLCAPE values of around 1000 J/KG and DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG, the environment was favorable for these thunderstorms to produce strong to severe downburst wind gusts as well as areas of dense blowing dust across the dust prone areas.
episodes.206862: West-southwesterly wind flow across South Florida as Hurricane Erin passed well to the east in the Atlantic Ocean.
episodes.206872: Thunderstorms produced gusty winds along the coast south of Cape Canaveral and a waterspout east of Hobe Sound.
episodes.206914: A slow moving cold front encountering an environment displaying deep moisture and moderate instability supported thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall across Southeast South Carolina.
episodes.206915: A slow moving cold front encountering an environment displaying deep moisture and moderate instability supported thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.206928: Clusters of slow moving thunderstorms with embedded supercells developed within an environment of 40 kts of deep-layer shear and 2000 J/kg MLCAPE as a mid-level wave moved across the region. Isolated stronger storms had persistent enough updrafts to produce large hail, along with pockets of heavier rainfall of up to 5 to 7 inches in parts of Beadle County.
episodes.206936: Storms moving south across northeast South Dakota produced hail and heavy rain, leading to flash flooding around the Watertown area.||The resultant runoff would also later result in flooding of the Big Sioux and surrounding tributaries around the Watertown and Castlewood areas.
episodes.207066: Strong storms moving through western Minnesota produced high winds northwest of Ortonville, damaging trees at a farmstead near Thielke and Bentsen Lakes.
episodes.207067: Storms moved over portions of northeast South Dakota that had really no extra room for moisture from the preceding months of nearly constant rainfall. Thus, this moisture went straight into the Big Sioux and tributaries from the Watertown area down south to Castlewood. The COOP observer in Rauville would record 1.51 inches of rainfall pushing their monthly total up to 5.73 and a 3 month total of 23.32. The Watertown COOP would likewise come up with 1.86 inches, putting the monthly total at 5.85 and 20.1 for the preceding 3 months. Even Castlewood, while only topping out at 0.31 inches, would see their monthly total top out at 4.99 inches with a 3 month total of 22 inches.
episodes.207071: Strong thunderstorm winds occurred in Hughes County during the early morning hours of August 22nd.
episodes.207201: Thunderstorms initially moving westward toward southern Miami-Dade County collided with a southward-moving outflow boundary along the coastline.  A large thunderstorm development at the collision point moving southwest along the nearshore waters of Key Largo.

events.narrative: The parking lot and first floor hotel rooms of the Extended Stay America Hotel were evacuated due to a culvert running under Frontage Road NW backing up across the hotel property.  This was due to between 4 and 5 inches of rain falling within a 2 hour period in the local area.  Video recorded by a hotel patron showed water in the parking lot up to 2 feet deep.  Some of the hotel rooms had water intrusion.
Runoff from 4 to 5 of rainfall was observed flowing several inches deep across Ring Road near the Valley View Mall.

A trained spotter surveying for damage reported multiple trees topped, uprooted or damaged at a farmstead northeast of Ortonville. Minor structural damage to a small grain bin and outbuilding included shingles torn from the roof.
A USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt (AFHA3) recorded a rise of 5.91 feet.
A 68 mph peak gust was measured at a mesonet site in Tortilla Flat.
Report of quarter size hail. Time estimated by radar.
Images showed power poles toppled near Gold Canyon. Location and timing based on outage map report. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed power lines in Apache Junction. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Numerous RV and mobile homes located along Greenfield Rd between Main Street and Broadway Road in Mesa sustained damage. The damages reported were from car ports, metal awnings, and downed trees. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 60 mph. No injuries were reported.

Carson Street in Pilot Mountain, NC is was observed flooded around 1 foot deep as runoff from heavy rain overflowed a drainage ditch across the roadway, making the road impassible to traffic.  The road was reopened to traffic after the water receded.
A portion of Old NC Highway 52 was damaged by flooding in the Town of King.  Several homes in the nearby area also suffered some degree of water intrusion due to the flooding.
A 69 mph peak gust was measured at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.

Heavy rainfall on saturated soils resulted in flooding in and around Watertown, with street flooding reported across the city. Northeast of Watertown, a vehicle left the Interstate after encountering some 10 inches of water on the roadway that flooded both  lanes near mile marker 182. When emergency crews arrived, the car was barely visible, with only the rear bumper above water. The occupant of the car swam to safety, was checked out on the scene by paramedics, but did not require any further medical attention.|Due to flooding, Interstate 29 was shut down between Exit 181 and Exit 185.

Large tree fell on top of a couple parked vehicles and caused damage to a carport at Las Brisas Condominiums near 7th Street and Northern Ave in Phoenix with another large tree uprooted along a canal located near the condominium. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Several downed trees near 12th Street and Northern Ave in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
A very large tree uprooted near the area of 3rd street and Northern Avenue in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Downed palm tree in the vicinity of 7th street and I-10 in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 65 mph. No injuries were reported.
Reported downed powerlines in the area of 11th to 14th street near the vicinity of Glendale Avenue in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 65 mph. No injuries were reported.

Willow Creek near Watertown went into flood on the evening of August 21st, topping out at 12.86 feet, or 2.86 feet above flood stage during the early morning hours of August 22nd before slowly falling, dropping below flood stage at 1230 AM August 23rd.
Much of a one-mile stretch of 196th Street was inundated by water east of 409th Avenue. Several  other county gravel roads had sections under water.
Hail caused significant damage to vehicles.

The South Branch Tributary Mud Creek near Rauville went into flood during the early morning hours of August 22nd, cresting at 4.91 feet, 0.91 feet above flood stage around mid-day. The creek would remain in flood through the early afternoon of August 23rd.
